# Actual group cap flux and a directional inverse-defect payment

This extends the independently audited geometric-group flux to actual allocated caps. It then conditions the common physical defect budget by its actual exterior normal, while retaining the entire cap law. The resulting inverse-defect moment inequality no longer needs the whole cap law to have one source gradient, an irreducible circuit, or an affine graph of fiber centers. It still provides no universal lower bound on the captured term, and therefore no OC numerical conclusion.

Dependencies, with their hypotheses retained:

* `candidate e90eb0947d2b9feb`, independently audited in `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`;
* `candidate 91145d6ea212266a`;
* `candidate 942ae5a91bb1a792`.

The nontrivial setting is `d>=2`. Under the bounded inverse-mass hypotheses the `d<=1` defect cases are trivial, as explained in the first dependency.

## 1. Actual cell traces for one allocated cap

Work first in one fiber, with its actual convex active cells `C_ij`, and a fixed limiting positive-proportionality group `G`. Its limiting affine gradients have the common direction `e`, so `c_i=|c_i|e` for `i in G`. All inverse, boundary, and section measures below retain their actual exponential rate and physical position. Write `mu_G` for the projection of this group's full exterior surface-log defect, forgetting its determined normal `-e`. Let

    N_G = M sum_{i in G} |c_i| zetahat_i.

The audited full group identity is `N_G=K mu_G`, where `K` keeps physical position fixed and sends rate `R` to the uniform law `U_R` on `[0,R]`, with `U_0=delta_0`.

Retain one actual cap record `H_j={a_j.z+u_j.X>=t_j}`, converging to `H`, with the established bounded record hypotheses and `|u_j|` bounded below. Its body selector and allocated coarea measure are the original all-status selectors. We use three actual group restrictions:

1. On the exterior boundary, multiply the body selector by the group's interior trace from `K_j`.
2. In volume, restrict each geometric cell inverse measure to the actual cap `H_j`.
3. On a proper cap section, use the group's trace from the interior of `K_j intersect H_j`. At an inside or outside supporting cap, use the group's interior trace from `K_j` and the original section allocation.

The resulting full zero-set defects are denoted `alpha_G,H`, `zetahat_i^H`, and `s_G,H`, respectively. They are positive and obtained by joint compactification of these actual selectors. In particular

    0<=alpha_G,H<=mu_G,   0<=zetahat_i^H<=zetahat_i.

There is no replacement by a limiting closed-halfspace bit on the zero set. Put

    N_G,H = M sum_{i in G} |c_i| zetahat_i^H.

To justify the section convention, partition the actual proper cap body by the interiors of its active cells. Gauss--Green on this partition uses the trace from the cap interior on its exposed cap boundary. A coincident cell interface and cap plane is counted once, as that exposed boundary. Interfaces lying strictly inside the cap have opposite normals and cancel. If the coincident interface separates different groups, its logarithmic tail is uniformly integrable by the group theorem, so any choice of its ordinary all-status allocation makes no difference to the defect identity. If it separates cells of the same group, the group trace agrees on both sides. At global inside support the body and section allocations sum to one; at global outside support they coincide, so the same group trace preserves the original allocated identity. These observations also cover fractional supporting allocations.

## 2. Exact vector and scalar cap fluxes

For a positive integer `m`, sum allocated Gauss--Green over the cap-restricted cells of `G`, using `phi ell_j r_j^m`, where `ell_j=(-log L_j)_+`. The internal interfaces cancel. Intergroup interface terms, even after cap restriction, tend to zero by the uniform logarithmic tail bound. The bulk test-gradient term tends to zero by bulk-log uniform integrability. The cap section term retains its original sign and allocated coarea. Consequently

    -int phi n r^m d ahat_G,H
      = M(m+1) sum_{i in G} c_i int phi r^m d zetahat_i^H
           -u int phi r^m d s_G,H.                  (1)

Here `ahat_G,H` retains the actual exterior normal; its projection is `alpha_G,H`. It is a submeasure of the group's full defect, so its normal is exactly `-e`.

For the zeroth moment repeat the group's audited tail proof with `F_j,T=(ell_j-T)_+`. Cap restriction only reduces the bulk and intergroup tail bounds. The allocated section logarithmic masses are bounded, and their ordinary logarithmic traces are integrable by the capwise dependency. Thus the same continuous factor `q_T(L_j)`, extended by one for nonpositive arguments, passes the body and section limits. Passing low-level inverse indicators along a cofinal sequence of continuity levels, then letting `T` increase, proves (1) also for `m=0`. In that formula the zeroth monomial means the constant function one, including rate zero.

The group section defect is zero unless `u` is parallel to `e`. Indeed on a group cell the section logarithm is the restriction of `A_ij`; if `u` is not parallel to `c_i`, its tangential gradient on the cap plane has a uniform positive lower bound. Coarea in the bounded cap plane bounds its logarithmic tail by `C int_0^epsilon(-log s) ds`. The coarea normalization `1/|u_j|` is uniformly bounded. There are finitely many cells. In the parallel case, a nonzero group section defect also forces the limiting cap plane to be the group's affine zero plane in that fiber. The sign `u=+|u|e` is then inside support, and `u=-|u|e` is outside support.

Set `kappa_H=e.u`. Because `s_G,H=0` when `u` is not parallel to `e`, projection of (1) onto `e` yields, for every `m>=0`,

    int phi r^m d alpha_G,H
       = (m+1) int phi r^m d N_G,H
            -kappa_H int phi r^m d s_G,H.           (2)

Compact moment uniqueness gives the exact signed-kernel identity

    N_G,H = K(alpha_G,H + kappa_H s_G,H).            (3)

The measure inside the kernel need not be positive when the exception is outside. The actual measure on the left is always positive. When there is no section defect, (3) is a positive capwise uniform kernel.

For complementary actual records, exterior selectors and volume restrictions add to their full-body counterparts. The section defects are equal: their group traces can differ only on an intergroup interface coinciding with the cap plane, whose logarithmic defect is zero. Inside/outside allocations use the same section measure. Thus

    alpha_G,H+alpha_G,Hc=mu_G,
    N_G,H+N_G,Hc=N_G,
    s_G,Hc=s_G,H.

The complementary normal changes sign, and the two section terms in (3) cancel, recovering the group kernel.

## 3. Which conditioning of the common budget is legitimate

Return to the finite family of integer fibers. There are finitely many nonzero limiting continuous gradient directions. Every exterior logarithmic defect has normal equal to the negative of one of these directions, by the audited geometric normal rigidity.

Fix one oriented direction `e`. Sum the actual geometric group defects over every fiber and every group with this direction. Denote the aggregated measures by

    mu_e, N_e, alpha_e,H, N_e,H, s_e,H.

The kernels and cap fluxes from Sections 1-2 add, with the same scalar `kappa_H=e.u_H`. In a single fiber, two relevant groups with the same direction cannot have different zero planes: both planes support the same positive body on the same side, so their zero levels agree and they were one group. Across distinct integer fibers the zero planes can differ; the present aggregation retains all of them.

Let `theta` be the SAME full probability law of actual cap records used by the physical separator. All needed limits are joint with that law. No sublaw is renormalized or selected. The cap-load measure is

    alpha_e = int alpha_e,H dtheta(H).

Choose a continuous nonnegative normal test `psi_e` which is one at `-e` and zero at all other finitely many defect normal directions. The common scale-resolved defect budget then gives

    int f(w) g(r) d alpha_e
        +int f(w) r g(r) d mu_e
       <= beta int f(w) g(r) d mu_e,                (4)

for every nonnegative finite convex physical `f` and every nonnegative convex nondecreasing rate `g`. The reserve is exactly `r mu_e`.

This is genuine normal conditioning. It conditions neither on an arbitrary source row, a selected cap circuit, a single fiber, nor a subset of groups with the same direction. The test `f` remains a globally admissible convex physical test. In particular arbitrary fiber indicators cannot be inserted.

## 4. Exact directional moment payment

Let `E_+(e)` be the actual cap records whose continuous normal is a positive multiple of `e`. These are the only possible inside section exceptions for this direction. Define

    N_e^noninside = int_{H notin E_+(e)} N_e,H dtheta(H).

This is a positive submeasure of `N_e`. It uses actual cap selections at every boundary incidence.

For a nonnegative physical test `f`, write `T_m(D)=int f r^m dD`, with `T_0(D)=int f dD`. Equations (2)-(3) imply

    T_m(alpha_e,H) = (m+1)T_m(N_e,H) - kappa_H T_m(s_e,H).       (5)

If `H` is not an inside exception, the last term is nonnegative or zero. If it is an inside exception, `alpha_e,H` is still positive, so its entire contribution can be dropped without introducing a negative remainder. Therefore

    T_m(alpha_e) >= (m+1)T_m(N_e^noninside).        (6)

Apply (4) with `g=1` for `m=0`, and `g(r)=r^m` for integers `m>=1`. The full group kernel gives

    T_m(mu_e)=(m+1)T_m(N_e),
    T_{m+1}(mu_e)=(m+2)T_{m+1}(N_e).

Substituting these exact factors and (6) proves

    T_m(N_e^noninside)
       + [(m+2)/(m+1)] T_{m+1}(N_e)
        <= beta T_m(N_e),   every integer m>=0.    (7)

In particular,

    int f dN_e^noninside + 2 int f r dN_e
        <= beta int f dN_e.                       (8)

The second term is the rate reserve measured on the inverse defect. Its factor two is necessary: it is the first-moment factor of the uniform kernel. The result retains the exact `beta`; no dimension factor has been lost.

More information remains available before dropping inside exceptions. Equations (4)-(5) give

    (m+1) T_m(int N_e,H dtheta)
       -int kappa_H T_m(s_e,H) dtheta
       +(m+2) T_{m+1}(N_e)
        <= beta(m+1) T_m(N_e).                    (9)

For each inside exception, positivity of its body term gives

    |u_H| T_m(s_e,H) <= (m+1) T_m(N_e,H).          (10)

An outside exception has the opposite sign and increases the cost. These statements are weighted moment inequalities, not an assertion that a signed measure before the kernel is positive at every rate.

## 5. A checkable atomic consequence, and the remaining numerical issue

Suppose the direction-`e` exterior defect is supported over a single physical point `w_*` and one positive surface rate `R`, with mass `B>0`. Then

    mu_e = B delta_(w_*,R),
    N_e = B delta_w* U_R.

If `C` is a collection of actual cap records outside `E_+(e)` whose limiting margins at `w_*` are strictly positive, stability of those strict margins forces `N_e,H=N_e` for each such record. Let `p=theta(C)`. The remaining selected measures are positive, so (7), or just (8), yields

    p + R <= beta.                                (11)

This conclusion uses the actual full cap weights. It remains valid if all other cap margins are incident and their selections unresolved, since those contributions were only dropped. In an irreducible full-rank finite cap circuit there is at most one record parallel to `e`, so only that one record can be omitted as an inside exception.

No lower bound `p>=beta` has been proved. A positive circuit alone can assign an arbitrarily small positive weight to its strictly capturing record; the archived simplex calibration likewise warns against presuming high cap load at a zero vertex. Thus (11) is a real incidence/rate restriction, not yet a contradiction. Establishing a lower bound on the actual captured inverse-defect term from deepestness, contact rows, and the complete lattice base is the next missing step.

## 6. A legitimate bridge to source rows, and its precise limitation

There is a useful aggregate identification with the actual contact-row labels. It does not permit arbitrary source conditioning. Use the finite source-plane presentation from `candidate 8ba63f3af7e6943f`. At each index its actual inverse rows are

    nu_ij = (sigma_ij/L_ij) rho_ij,
    sum_i nu_ij = dm_j/(M_j L_j),

and row `i` is supported on `A_ij=L_j`. Every `nu_ij` is absolutely continuous with respect to the full current inverse volume measure, since it is a positive summand. At almost every point of such a row the parameter is differentiable in the continuous variables, and its continuous gradient is exactly `c_ij`.

Fix a nonzero limiting oriented direction `e`, and let `I_e` be all surviving source labels with `c_i/|c_i|=e`. Labels with different limiting directions, or with limiting gradient zero, have distinct current continuous gradients from the labels in `I_e` for all sufficiently large `j`. On a full-dimensional geometric cell, every source label that charges it therefore has the same current continuous gradient as that cell. If several source planes coincide on a fiber, their continuous gradients coincide and their positive row densities add to the geometric inverse density there. It follows, as actual prelimit measures, that

    sum_{i in I_e} |c_ij| nu_ij

equals the sum of `|c_cell,j|` times the geometric cell inverse measures over cells whose selected source plane has its limiting direction in `e`. Multiplying both sides by the same actual rate record, or restricting both sides to the same actual cap, preserves this equality. Passing joint limits and restricting to the zero set gives

    N_e = M sum_{i in I_e} |c_i| zetahat_i^source,
    N_e,H = M sum_{i in I_e} |c_i| zetahat_i^{source,H}.            (12)

These identities merge all source labels with the direction. They do not split the boundary measure among individual rows, and do not identify a row with a geometric group. A prelimit label of vanishing source weight has vanishing inverse mass by the marked-value floor, so it leaves no missing term.

In particular the physical first moment of the full directional inverse defect is determined by the actual source rows:

    int (1,w) dN_e
      = M sum_{i in I_e} (sigma_i |c_i|/L_i)(1,Y_i)
          -int_{grad_X L has direction e}
                    [|grad_X L|/L](1,w) dm.                      (13)

The ordinary integral is finite. The identity keeps the boundary defect and the full integer-coordinate moments; it is not an original-volume martingale assertion.

For an own-source cap through `Y_i=(p_i,y_i)` in the ordinary limit, write its margin as

    m_H(z,X)=a_H.(z-p_i)+u_H.(X-y_i),
    A_i(z,X)=L_i+a_i.(z-p_i)+c_i.(X-y_i).

If `u_H=t c_i` with `t>0`, then on this row's zero face `A_i=0`,

    m_H(z,X)=-t L_i+(a_H-t a_i).(z-p_i).            (14)

Thus the own-source fiber `z=p_i` is strictly missed, but other target fibers need not be. The row martingale fixes the integer mean of the ENTIRE row, not of its zero-set component alone. Its ordinary and defect integer moments can compensate, as (13) explicitly records. Consequently (14) does not justify removing all positive-parallel capture from a source row.

Finally, the captured term in (7) is the actual full-law cross mixture

    int_{H notin E_+(e)} sum_{i in I_e}
                M |c_i| zetahat_i^{source,H} dtheta(H).          (15)

The cap law and the source-row weights are different marginals of the same certificate. Formula (15) is not a diagonal sum pairing each row only with its own source caps. A lower bound obtained solely for such diagonal pairs would need a further proved argument to control (15). This is the specific remaining compatibility issue, rather than an unspecified freedom to condition a source group.
